fullPassage: Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that reading aloud lights up many areas of the brain. There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you to read each and every word — something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should be encouraged to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and reading aloud.

det.tip: positive(긍정적인) ↔ negative(부정적인). 가장 기본적인 반의어 쌍 중 하나

questions.passage: Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that reading aloud lights up many <u><u>area</u>s</u> of the brain. There is intense activity in <u>areas</u> associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you to read each and every word — something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should be encouraged to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and reading aloud.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 <u>areas</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 뇌의 여러 영역을 활성화한다 / (B) 새 공원의 전체 면적은 약 500제곱미터이다
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 지역은 지리적 장소에 해당하여 뇌 맥락에 부적절
✅ ② (A) 영역(뇌의 특정 부분) — (B) 면적(물리적 넓이): 각 문맥에 적합 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 분야는 학문 맥락이라 뇌 영역과 다름
❌ ④ (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜
det.tip: area의 다의어: 영역(특정 부분), 면적(넓이), 지역(장소), 분야(학문 등)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"the way in which words are spoken or made, especially in a particular language or by a particular person"

det.korean: 단어가 발화되거나 만들어지는 방식, 특히 특정 언어나 특정 사람에 의한 것
det.analysis:
❌ ① pronunciation(발음): 단어를 말하는 방식이라는 정의에 정확히 부합
❌ ② concentration(집중력): 주의를 집중하는 능력으로 의미 다름
✅ ③ stimulation(자극): 활성화나 자극을 의미하므로 부적절
❌ ④ imagination(상상력): 머릿속으로 그리는 능력이므로 부적절
det.tip: pronounce(발음하다) → pronunciation(발음). -tion 접미사가 붙은 명사형

questions.passage: There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the __________ (connect) structures of your brain cells for more brainpower.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로).

det.korean: 발음과 관련된 영역의 활동이 뇌세포의 연결 구조를 강화한다.
det.analysis: connect → connective(형용사): structures(구조)를 수식하는 형용사 형태가 필요. connect(동사) → connective(연결하는, 형용사)
det.tip: connect(동사) → connective(형용사): '연결하는'이라는 의미의 형용사로 변환. connection(명사)과 혼동 주의

questions.passage: Children, in particular, should be __________ (encourage) to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로).

det.korean: 특히 아이들은 소리 내어 읽도록 격려받아야 한다.
det.analysis: encourage → encouraged(과거분사): 'should be + p.p.' 수동태 구문에서 과거분사가 필요. encourage(동사) → encouraged(과거분사)
det.tip: should be __________ 구문은 수동태(be + p.p.). 주어(Children)가 격려를 '받는' 대상이므로 수동태 encouraged가 정답

questions.passage: Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that reading aloud lights up many areas of the brain. There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your __________ because it forces you to read each and every word — something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should be encouraged to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as singing, touching, and reading aloud.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소리 내어 읽기는 또한 대중 연설 기술을 발전시키는 좋은 방법이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① public speaking skills(대중 연설 기술): 모든 단어를 읽도록 강제하기 때문에 대중 연설 기술을 발전시킨다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② brain-scanning techniques(뇌 스캔 기법): 연구 방법이지 발전시킬 대상이 아님
✅ ③ connective structures(연결 구조): 뇌세포의 구조이며 이 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ positive stimulation(긍정적 자극): 학습의 원인이지 발전시킬 대상이 아님
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤의 'because it forces you to read each and every word'가 대중 연설과 연결되는 핵심 단서

questions.passage: Modern brain-scanning techniques such as fMRI (functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging) have revealed that reading aloud lights up many areas of the brain. There is intense activity in areas associated with pronunciation and hearing the sound of the spoken response, which strengthens the connective structures of your brain cells for more brainpower. This leads to an overall improvement in concentration. Reading aloud is also a good way to develop your public speaking skills because it forces you to read each and every word — something people don't often do when reading quickly, or reading in silence. Children, in particular, should be encouraged to read aloud because the brain is wired for learning through connections that are created by positive stimulation, such as __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뇌는 노래, 접촉, 소리 내어 읽기와 같은 긍정적 자극에 의해 만들어지는 연결을 통해 학습하도록 연결되어 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ② singing, touching, and reading aloud(노래, 접촉, 소리 내어 읽기): 긍정적 자극의 예시로 such as 뒤에 오는 구체적 활동들
✅ ① reading quickly, or reading in silence(빨리 읽기, 조용히 읽기): 소리 내어 읽기와 대비되는 활동으로 '긍정적 자극'의 예시에 부적절
❌ ③ wired for learning(학습을 위해 연결된): 뇌의 상태를 설명하는 구로 자극의 예시 아님
❌ ④ many areas of the brain(뇌의 많은 영역): 장소 표현으로 자극의 예시 아님
det.tip: such as 뒤에는 앞의 개념의 구체적 예시가 와야 함. positive stimulation의 예시를 찾기

ch: reading quickly, or reading in silence
